_note: Reads of a column that is absent from db/schema_snapshot.json and are DELIBERATE FORWARD-COMPATIBILITY rather than defects. Keyed on (file, property) -- the same convention as tools/fail_open_accepted.json, and for the same reason: a line number shifts on every edit and a stale line silently un-accepts an entry. AN ACCEPTANCE IS NOT AN EXEMPTION FROM THE QUESTION, it is a recorded answer to it, so every entry carries the EVIDENCE that the absent column is handled rather than a promise that it is. An entry matching nothing in the current source is reported as STALE by the checker and is a finding in its own right -- an acceptance that outlives the code it excused is how a gate stops covering anything. The bar: the read must normalise an absent column to a value the CALL SITES treat as a third state, and a named test must pin that. 'It degrades to null' is not sufficient on its own -- null has to mean CANNOT-TELL somewhere, not 'no'. THE LINE THAT DECIDES IT, established 2026-09-16 by nearly getting it wrong: `api/_lib/license.js` reads TWO absent columns and only ONE of them belongs here. `trial_ends_at` is REFUSED -- null there means NOT EXPIRED, which is one of the two answers, so the trial gate cannot fire and that is the founding finding this whole tool was written for (see its own docstring). `subscription_status` is ACCEPTED -- null there is explicitly CANNOT-TELL, is neither answer, and is pinned in both directions by a named test. Degrading to null is not the test; what null MEANS at the call site is.

reason: ADDED 2026-09-15 (item 100) WITH THE ABSENCE STATED IN ITS OWN COMMENT: 'THIS COLUMN DOES NOT EXIST TODAY AND NOTHING IS INVENTED BY READING IT.' The defect it fixes is the opposite of a fabrication -- three handlers derived a paid tier from the mere presence of `stripe_subscription_id`, which a cancelled subscription keeps for ever, so the gate could grant and could never revoke. An IDENTIFIER IS NOT A STATE. EVIDENCE THAT NULL MEANS CANNOT-TELL, and this is the arm that protects real subscribers: api/license-trial-gate.test.js 'CANNOT-TELL is NOT refused -- an id with no state column is the case today' asserts that a subscribed licence with a null status and an expired trial is NOT refused, because with no status column EVERY subscribed licence is in that state right now. Its sibling 'CANNOT-TELL is not GRANTED either' pins that an unrecognised status also falls through, so knownPaid and knownNotPaid are explicitly NOT complements. Folding cannot-tell into either answer would 402 every paying customer the day trial_ends_at is added and this column is not.
